subthemes: Dead code, stale comments and small cleanups (37 entries, all low)
Duplication that a shared helper would absorb (43 entries: 6 medium, 37 low)
Oversized modules and proposed splits (5 entries, all low)

most_important.why: Three small (effort S) backend fixes with the largest wall-clock payoff on big tenants: a bypassed single-flight gate that triggers duplicate full /applications and /servicePrincipals scans, a credential-only bulk sweep that busts both tenant-wide indexes, and a read-through cache attached to the cheap per-SP read instead of the tenant-wide appRoleAssignedTo read that dominates the audit and consent view.

The only finding with a hard external deadline: KEYVAULT_API 2023-07-01 stops working on 2027-02-27 (all control-plane versions before 2026-02-01 retire, no exception); one-line bump plus a source/review-date comment.

The /token POST has no retry while every other client honours core::http_retry; a transient 429/5xx becomes a terminal token_exchange and a launch-time blip forces a full browser sign-in although the keyring token is fine.

The one large-effort item and a root cause: every mutation rebuilds the whole detail pane, re-running every visited tab's IPC resources, discarding forms, and forcing the credentials tab's three deferred-reload workarounds.

The advanced-query flag differs between page 1 and continuations at ten call sites (and is inverted for the SP index), so multi-page security reads mix the primary and eventually consistent stores; the transport's own history shows this drift already produced a silent wrong answer once.

Five medium frontend findings share one pattern: documented primitives (DetailLoadError, DirectorySearch, Badge, DataTable) are bypassed at dozens of sites, which is how a nonexistent badge--info tone, a regressed 'No matches' bug and missing table keynav shipped; each proposal includes a repo_invariants scan to stop re-accumulation.

result.summary: The cleanup, refactor, performance and dependency bucket holds 114 findings (0 high, 14 medium, 100 low; 83 confirmed, 31 partially confirmed), merged into 106 entries after eight same-file duplicates. The dominant theme is duplication: 43 entries describe documented primitives or shared cores (DetailLoadError, DirectorySearch, Badge, DataTable, UiError::not_found, thumbprint::canonical, collect_pages_from) that later code re-implemented by hand, with several proposals adding repo_invariants scans to stop the drift recurring. Performance carries seven of the fourteen medium findings, all avoidable network work rather than hot loops: a bypassed single-flight gate (F007), over-broad cache invalidation on a bulk sweep (F026), a grant cache attached to the wrong Graph read (F179), a doubled SSO Graph chain (F375), an unretried token endpoint (F111) and a detail pane that remounts every tab per mutation (F336, the only large-effort item). Dependency hygiene is mostly manifest honesty (six unused declarations, bytes and keyring-core outside the workspace table, over-wide tokio and futures features), plus one dated item: the Key Vault control-plane api-version retires on 2027-02-27 (F257). Dead code clusters around blanket lint allows in web-rs bindings and components, stale docs after the resource-aware and directory-module refactors, and leftovers from removed features (kv_set_secret, export_audit_csv, the command palette CSS, the gallery partial flag). Three command files (audit.rs, permissions.rs, sso/mod.rs) exceed 1400 lines and the repo has already proven the directory-module split twice. The verifier corrections were kept throughout: notably the thiserror re-export idea is infeasible (F214/F226), the Exchange is_retryable method is live via the dto macro (F177), and the sign-out sweep and posture 'exactly once' claims were narrower than first reported (F046, F401). Ninety of the 114 findings are effort S, so most of this bucket is mechanical.

subthemes: Remediation and tenant mutations with the wrong outcome
Configuration, cloud environment and updater controls
Robustness, error classification and UI state

most_important.why: Org-wide Graph MailboxItem.*/MailboxFolder.*/Mail-Advanced.* grants (tenant-wide mailbox content read/write/export) score zero and raise no mailbox finding; a silent false negative in the exact class the audit exists to catch.

The SSO claims editor both writes transformation policies that can never be emitted and, when the policy read is unconsented, shows an empty editor whose Save detaches the app's live claims policy; a data-destroying no-op save on a security-critical surface.

DR backup Pass 3 returns an Ok manifest with every managed identity's roles empty on a dead session, and the restore UI/runbook tells the operator to re-run a restore that duplicates every app with fresh secrets and consent; the DR path can silently lose data and then multiply trust in the destination.

Three remediation surfaces report success while the org-wide grant or legacy policy is still in place (partial AAP migration toasts Migrated, SP-path scope warnings are dropped, vetoed redundant-permission removals vanish from the Fix button), inviting operators to remove the only remaining confinement.

Coverage is overstated on security-posture views: a >5000-site tenant's Sites.Selected sweep is cached as complete and affirms no per-site grants, and the EWS full_access_as_app grant never receives a scope verdict so a correctly RBAC-scoped EWS app still scores org-wide.

Two advertised configuration controls are inert: the documented auto-update opt-out (an MDM/no-egress promise) is never read, and a domain-form tenant id the config screen accepts can never sign in, with a misleading token_exchange hint.

Session-security regressions in the auth service: Graph adapters consume non-CAE tokens seeded by every interactive flow (losing prompt revocation), a per-resource MFA step-up purges the whole session, and a failed keyring delete on sign-out leaves the restore pointer and refresh token in place.

result.summary: The bugs-and-security bucket holds 113 verified findings (12 high, 58 medium, 43 low; 87 confirmed, 26 partially), consolidated into 103 entries after merging nine duplicate groups. The dominant theme is results that mislead the operator in the conservative-looking direction: the mailbox advisory misses the newer RBAC-scopable Graph permissions, the EWS scope never gets a verdict, the Sites.Selected sweep and several permission-tester paths report unreadable or truncated data as clean, and the DR backup can return a complete-looking manifest with empty managed-identity roles. A second cluster is tenant mutations whose reported outcome diverges from what landed: the claims codec writes unusable transformation policies and an unread policy is detached on Save, partial AAP migrations toast success, warnings and vetoes are dropped, and several create/grant cores return Err after real writes so caches go stale and retries duplicate. Auth and session findings are mostly medium: CAE tokens are never actually minted for Graph adapters, interaction_required purges the whole session, sign-out ordering can fail open, and two documented controls (auto-update opt-out, domain-form tenant id) are inert end to end. The 21 security-tagged findings are almost all low-severity least-privilege and defense-in-depth hygiene (unused CSP origins and plugin capabilities, signing-key scope during build, un-zeroized key copy, unvalidated ARM ids, raw error bodies in logs); the one medium is the Key Vault browser surviving a tenant switch. Robustness items include a WASM-wide panic on any non-UiError IPC rejection, a throttle that halves only once, and a fresh-clone `just setup` that panics before the frontend dist exists. Most fixes are small (effort S dominates), and many can be pinned with the repo's existing repo_invariants pattern.

subthemes: Docs drift: claim vs code, grouped by document (AGENTS.md and .claude/rules; README/SECURITY/.github; docs/architecture deep-dives; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and setup scripts; doc comments inside the code)

Test gaps by crate and tier (src-tauri commands and repo invariants; web-rs GUI tests, native tests and demo fixtures; azapptoolkit-auth; azapptoolkit-core; azapptoolkit-graph; azapptoolkit-exchange and azapptoolkit-keyvault)

most_important.why: AGENTS.md sends every contributor to these architecture docs before touching auth, Exchange scoping or the scope wizard, and each currently instructs them to write code the repo's own invariants forbid or reject (recreate two matches! lists, call deleted value-only scoping functions, assume three touch points where about ten exist).

The browser GUI suite is the frontend's only behavioural gate, yet it never mounts the trust-minting and full-collection-write surfaces (federated credentials, Expose an API, SSO wizard, create app, Permissions/Owners actions), never renders a cancelled or truncated audit run, and asserts no ARIA state value, so the documented boolean-attribute bug keeps recurring.

Three mechanical pins are missing or lenient: docs-only PRs skip the tests that pin AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the commit hook; IPC parity has only an always-exit-0 hook; and the trust/redirect validation rules check the validator per module, the exact helper bleed the invariant suite was rewritten to remove.

An operator provisioned exactly per the published custom role gets 403 on README-advertised SAML rollover, claims mapping, SP owner and delete flows, and the capabilities catalog (the single source for readiness, RequiresRole labels and 403 hints) has no rows for the policy_write and sync scopes.

Four one-line primitive fixes remove most of the a11y debt at once: string-valued aria-expanded on FilterToggle and the account menu, aria-pressed on FilterChip (14 sites), role=alert on DetailLoadError and a FormError primitive (66 sites), and row-specific names on per-row destructive buttons.

Security-relevant library contracts are unpinned: the interactive auth flow (tid, nonce, consent identity, reauth) is untestable without a launcher seam, the graph crate has no test that a POST is not replayed after a 502 (the addPassword double-mint incident), several hard-won Graph client contracts have zero wiremock coverage, the Key Vault off-origin refusal and exp serialisation are untested, and Exchange's hand-rolled error table has no conformance test.

result.summary: This bucket holds 103 verified findings (0 high, 31 medium, 72 low); two same-file duplicates were merged (F313 with F362, F014 with F245), giving 101 entries. Documentation drift is broad rather than deep: the architecture deep-dives that AGENTS.md makes mandatory reading now contradict the code and AGENTS.md itself on the BearerProvider boundary, the re-auth-fatal code list, the deleted value-only Exchange scoping functions and the scope-wizard extension recipe, and roughly twenty doc comments, runbooks and workflow comments describe pre-refactor shapes. The README, the operator custom role and the capabilities catalog omit shipped features or the permissions and scopes behind them, which leaves a per-the-docs operator hitting 403s on advertised SAML flows. Test coverage is strong where table-driven pure helpers exist and thin at the seams: mutation-heavy frontend surfaces have zero GUI coverage, no GUI test renders a partial audit run or asserts an ARIA state, handler-level backend tests exist only for add_password_core, and the auth crate's interactive flow is untestable without a launcher seam. Several invariant pins are missing or lenient (IPC parity, per-command trust validation, the $top rule, the audit cache guard), and the CI change detector skips exactly the tests that pin AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the commit hook. Tooling gaps are hygiene-level (no rustdoc, unused-dependency or pedantic clippy gate; just check omits the test harness). Accessibility findings concentrate in shared primitives, so four one-line changes (string aria-expanded, aria-pressed on FilterChip, role=alert on DetailLoadError, row-specific button names) plus one GUI assertion module would fix most sites and stop the recurring boolean-attribute bug.

subthemes: Scoping (Exchange and SharePoint) and resource access
App registration editing: authentication, Expose an API, federation
Operator tooling: search, DR, settings, readiness
Graph API capabilities not yet adopted
Docs, demo, packaging and release tooling

most_important.why: The owner's own #109 design for a file-bridged posture snapshot and drift report is fully unblocked, every seam exists, and it turns the audit from a point-in-time view into the attestation trend question security committees ask; effort L, no new scopes or persistence policy.

The security workbench never reads federated identity credentials, the credential class the repo's own federation.rs doc calls the worst case (no secret, no expiry, silently accepted); the batched reader and validator already exist, so an advisory rule is a medium-effort closure of a real blind spot.

Both the audit run and the mailbox permission tester hide the realistic Exchange degraded mode (no admin rights or no consent): the audit lists RBAC-scoped apps as Critical with a Scope fix that will fail and caches the run as complete, and the tester's documented partial-coverage caveat can never fire.

Three scorer markers for unconfinable org-wide mailbox and SharePoint reach have no finding group, posture count or filter, so scored findings are invisible in the findings-first pane; the fix is small once the verifier's distinction between legacy-resource and unconfinable advice is respected.

Three one-definition-per-policy gaps in the shared plumbing: consent_required is flattened to token_error in every client so the shared consent fallback never fires for scoped calls, scoped writes bypass the retry loop entirely, and inner $batch 5xx sub-responses are terminal while the same GET alone is retried; each is effort S and affects many surfaces.

Destructive-action ergonomics on the write path: the bulk-delete copy claims irreversibility although Entra soft-deletes for 30 days and no recycle-bin surface exists, and SAML rotate/retire and 'Rotate & remove all secrets' run on one click while sibling actions are confirm-gated.

Two cheap Graph model additions the audit and CA tab miss today: workload-identity Conditional Access (clientApplications) is mis-reported in both directions for the tool's own subject, and disabledByMicrosoftStatus, Microsoft's own malicious-app flag, is not read though adjacent fields come from the same $select.

The DR manifest degrades per-SP assignment failures to empty with no skipped record, and the restore dry-run omits the schema blocker and every Pass 4/5 count plus the same-tenant duplicate warning, so the operator confirms against an incomplete plan.

result.summary: This bucket holds 108 verified enhancement and feature findings, none high, 30 medium and 78 low; two same-file pairs were merged (F042 with F428, F264 with F276), giving 106 entries. Two-thirds were confirmed as stated and 42 carry a verifier correction, most often a severity downgrade, a wrong line citation, or an overlooked existing mitigation such as a documented decision (single-tenant process, uncapped DataTable, deliberate kv_set_secret removal) that the entry now records. The strongest themes are visibility gaps rather than defects: degraded modes (Exchange unavailable, batch 5xx, consent_required, dead sessions) are handled correctly but not surfaced to the operator, and several scored audit signals have no home in the findings-first workbench. A second cluster is destructive-action ergonomics on the SSO and credential write paths (one-click rotate, retire and remove-all against confirm-gated siblings, and a bulk-delete message that contradicts Entra's 30-day soft delete). The Graph API section lists cheap, additive adoptions (disabledByMicrosoftStatus, workload-identity CA conditions, app management policies, requestSignatureVerification, SP risk detections, per-credential sign-in activity) that ride existing tokens and $select lists. The product-gap proposals keep their admin-value framing: the owner-designed drift report (#109) and a FIC audit rule are unblocked medium items, while headless CLI, in-process tenant switching and SP-credential dashboards are correctly scoped by the verifier as larger or invariant-sensitive. Operator tooling and readiness carry a coherent set of capability-catalog gaps (custom roles, sync and policy_write features, sovereign-cloud hosts, PIM eligibility) that one catalog pass could close together. The remaining low items are frontend consistency drift against documented primitives and small docs, demo and release-tooling improvements.
